tagline: DFKI is Germany's national AI research center, a non-profit public-private partnership founded in 1988 that turns academic research into industrial applications.
about: The German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence was established in 1988 as a non-profit public-private partnership. It began in Kaiserslautern and Saarbrücken, and Wolfgang Wahlster has served as its scientific director since the founding.

Today DFKI operates research facilities in Kaiserslautern, Saarbrücken, Bremen, Oldenburg and Osnabrück, laboratories in Berlin, Darmstadt and Lübeck, and a branch office in Trier. Its work is organized into 29 research departments, thirteen competence centers and eight living labs, and it is funded by the European Union, federal ministries, the German states and the German Research Foundation.

DFKI led the national Verbmobil project on speech translation, which produced several spin-off companies and earned the 2001 German Future Prize. Its public code and datasets appear on GitHub and Hugging Face, where researchers in several departments publish benchmarks and models.
mission: To conduct application-oriented AI research for industry and society and to transfer results into commercial software and spin-offs.
known_for: National AI research institute of Germany

tagline: The DTAI group at KU Leuven combines machine learning, logic and data mining and is the home of the RobBERT Dutch language models.
about: DTAI is the Declarative Languages and Artificial Intelligence research group in the Department of Computer Science at KU Leuven in Belgium. Its academic staff includes Hendrik Blockeel, Jesse Davis, Luc De Raedt, Tias Guns and Tom Schrijvers, and it is linked to the ADVISE, EAVISE and M-Group research groups.

In January 2020 researchers Pieter Delobelle, Thomas Winters and Bettina Berendt introduced RobBERT, a Dutch RoBERTa-based language model. The group has since refreshed it with RobBERT-2022 and RobBERT-2023, which are published under the DTAI-KULeuven organization on Hugging Face under the MIT license.
mission: To advance machine learning and reasoning methods and to supply open language resources for Dutch.
known_for: Machine learning combined with logic and constraints

tagline: EdinburghNLP is the University of Edinburgh's natural language processing group, ranked among the most productive in the world and the home of Nematus.
about: EdinburghNLP brings together faculty, postdocs and PhD students in the School of Informatics. Its research covers language modelling, morphology, parsing, semantics, discourse, generation and machine translation, with links to speech, vision and robotics.

The group reports a faculty of more than a dozen core members and five European Research Council grants, and it is ranked first for NLP output by csrankings.org. It publishes code and data openly, including the Nematus neural machine translation toolkit, the XSum summarization dataset and a widely used list of hallucination-detection papers.
mission: To develop algorithms that let computers understand and produce human language, and to share the resulting tools with the research community.

tagline: EleutherAI is a non-profit research institute that grew from a Discord server into a leading source of open language models, datasets and evaluation tools.
about: EleutherAI began in July 2020 as a Discord server under the working name LibreAI. Connor Leahy, Leo Gao and Sid Black are named as founders, and the group was renamed EleutherAI later that month. In early 2023 it was incorporated as a non-profit research institute.

It first used compute from Google's TPU Research Cloud and later from CoreWeave. The group released The Pile in December 2020, followed by the GPT-Neo, GPT-J and GPT-NeoX-20B models, and the Pythia suite for studying training dynamics.

Today it reports about fifteen full- and part-time staff along with regular volunteers. Its lm-evaluation-harness, the most starred repository in its GitHub organization, is used widely to benchmark language models.
mission: To advance interpretability and alignment research on open foundation models, keep such models open to study beyond a few companies, and educate the public about their capabilities and risks.

tagline: ELLIS Alicante is a non-profit unit of the European ELLIS network focused on ethical, human-centric AI, directed by Nuria Oliver.
about: ELLIS Alicante was founded in 2020 as a foundation hosting a research unit of the ELLIS network in Spain. It resulted from a 2019 bid, led by Nuria Oliver, for Alicante to host an ELLIS unit, and she serves as its director.

Its research addresses modeling human behavior at individual and societal scales, systems that interact naturally with people, and ethical AI covering fairness, privacy and transparency. It is funded by the Generalitat Valenciana, the European Regional Development Fund and partners including Intel and Fundación Banco Sabadell, and reports over 38 million euros in EU project budgets.

Paper code and evaluation repositories are published on GitHub, including tutorials on graph rewiring and fairness, an open framework for social media AR filters, and evaluations of how language models handle mental-health crises.
mission: To advance ethical, responsible and human-centric artificial intelligence that serves society.
known_for: Open benchmarks on fairness and LLM safety

tagline: The EPFL LLM team built Meditron, an open suite of medical language models, and the Megatron-LLM trainer used to produce them.
about: The EPFL LLM team is a group at the Swiss federal institute in Lausanne that publishes under the epfLLM GitHub and epfl-llm Hugging Face organizations. Its Megatron-LLM repository, created in July 2023, adapts NVIDIA's Megatron-LM trainer for distributed training of open models.

In November 2023 the team released MEDITRON, 7B and 70B-parameter medical models built on Llama-2 and further pretrained on PubMed papers, abstracts and international medical guidelines. The paper reports that MEDITRON-70B outperforms GPT-3.5 and Med-PaLM on four benchmarks, and the team released both model weights and the corpus-building code.
mission: To provide openly available medical language models and training tools so that clinical AI can be studied and improved in the open.

tagline: Flowers is an Inria team in Bordeaux studying curiosity-driven learning in humans and machines, led by Pierre-Yves Oudeyer.
about: The Flowers team investigates the mechanisms of sensorimotor, cognitive and social development in humans and machines. It is housed at Inria Bordeaux-Sud-Ouest and Univ. Bordeaux and is headed by Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, a research director known for work on artificial curiosity and intrinsic motivation.

The team's GitHub organization, opened in 2012, publishes research code such as the Explauto exploration library and testbeds for automatic curriculum learning in deep reinforcement learning. More recent releases ground language models in interactive environments using online reinforcement learning and provide the Lamorel library for that purpose.
mission: To understand how open-ended, curiosity-driven learning works and to build artificial agents that develop and learn in similar ways.

tagline: GPT-NL is a Dutch non-profit effort by TNO, NFI and SURF to build a lawful, sovereign Dutch language model trained on licensed data.
about: GPT-NL is a joint initiative of TNO, the Netherlands Forensic Institute and SURF, launched in November 2023 with a reported budget of 13.5 million euros. It aims to supply a language model for business and public use in which sovereignty, compliance and control matter.

The project stresses a clean data supply chain and has signed licensing arrangements with Dutch news publishers. It publishes datasets on Hugging Face, while its model is currently offered to launching customers, with GPT-NL version 1 scheduled for autumn 2026.
mission: To provide a Dutch-language model developed responsibly, with transparent and lawfully sourced training data, for use in the Netherlands.

tagline: GroNLP is the computational linguistics group at the University of Groningen, known for BERTje, HateBERT and Dutch GPT-2 models.
about: GroNLP is the Computational Linguistics group of the Center for Language and Cognition Groningen. Its members, including Malvina Nissim and Arianna Bisazza, work on topics from NLP to dialectology and publish models and datasets on Hugging Face.

In December 2019 the group introduced BERTje, a Dutch BERT model by Wietse de Vries, Andreas van Cranenburgh, Arianna Bisazza, Tommaso Caselli, Gertjan van Noord and Malvina Nissim. HateBERT, a BERT retrained for abusive language detection in English, followed in October 2020.
mission: To advance computational linguistics and give researchers open language models for Dutch and other languages.

tagline: Heidelberg NLP is the computational linguistics group at Heidelberg University, producing benchmarks such as VALSE and graph-based language models.
about: The Heidelberg Natural Language Processing Group is based at the Department of Computational Linguistics, where Anette Frank is among its principal researchers. Its GitHub organization, opened in 2019, hosts code for knowledge-graph extraction, multimodal explainability and model benchmarks.

Its releases include VALSE, a benchmark for vision and language models centered on linguistic phenomena, MM-SHAP for measuring multimodal contributions, and Graph Language Models, which Moritz Plenz and Anette Frank introduced in January 2024.
mission: To advance language understanding and make models more faithful and explainable through open benchmarks and methods.

tagline: HPLT is an EU-funded consortium coordinated by Charles University that publishes petabyte-scale multilingual web corpora and models.
about: High Performance Language Technologies is a three-year EU-funded project that started in September 2022. It is coordinated by Charles University in Prague and brings together five universities, two high-performance computing centers and a private NLP company.

Its first release covered monolingual data in 75 languages at 5.6 trillion tokens and parallel data in 18 language pairs. The second release reached 7.6 trillion tokens in 193 languages and 380 million parallel sentences in 51 pairs, distributed under the CC0 license on Hugging Face and its website.
mission: To provide open multilingual datasets, translation models and tools for training language models at scale.

tagline: The Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics' language technology group publishes the PULI Hungarian language models and national corpora.
about: The group grew from the Corpus Linguistics Department formed in 1997 and is led by Enikő Héja, with Gábor Prószéky and Tamás Váradi among its senior staff. It builds language resources, tools and neural models for Hungarian.

Its work includes the Hungarian National Corpus, completed in 2005 with a second edition in 2014, the e-magyar text processing system, and the HuLU benchmark modeled on GLUE. Its PULI family includes PULI-GPT-3SX, a seven-billion-parameter Hungarian model.
mission: To develop language technology for Hungarian, from corpora and morphology to modern neural language models.

tagline: Illuin Technology is a Paris AI company whose research team co-created ColPali visual document retrieval and the ViDoRe benchmark.
about: Illuin Technology is a Paris-based AI company that publishes research code under the illuin-tech GitHub organization and models on Hugging Face. Its researchers work with academic partners including CentraleSupélec and EPFL.

In February 2024 the team co-authored CroissantLLM, a 1.3B-parameter bilingual French-English model with open training data. In June 2024 it released ColPali, which retrieves documents using vision-language models, together with the ViDoRe benchmark, and in 2025 it followed with the ModernVBERT encoder under the MIT license.
mission: To build practical AI systems and advance open research on document understanding and retrieval.

tagline: IPI PAN, the Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences, publishes open Polish retrieval models and question answering datasets.
about: The Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences in Warsaw hosts a Linguistic Engineering Group that builds resources for Polish. Its researchers co-trained HerBERT with Allegro, and Alina Wróblewska is a co-author of that work.

Its Hugging Face organization lists dozens of models and datasets, including the PolQA and MAUPQA question answering datasets, the NKJP1M corpus, the Silver Retriever retrieval model, and HerBERT variants for Silesian and Kashubian.
mission: To provide open language resources and models for Polish and related regional languages.

tagline: JeRTeh is a Serbian society that releases Serbian language models, corpora and tools for language technology.
about: The Society for Language Resources and Technologies, known as JeRTeh, is a Serbian association that runs seminars, publishes resources and takes part in projects such as UniDive, Distant Reading, WikiELTeC and It-Sr-NER. It maintains a GitHub organization opened in 2023.

It publishes Serbian models such as Jerteh-355 on Hugging Face and corpora including srpELTeC. In April 2026 it joined a protocol with the Office for IT and eGovernment and ten other institutions to build a national Serbian language model.
mission: To develop and share language resources and models for Serbian.

tagline: The Language and Voice Lab at Reykjavik University builds open Icelandic speech corpora and recognition and synthesis models.
about: The Language and Voice Lab develops speech technology for Icelandic. It ran the crowd-sourced Samrómur corpus with Almannarómur, the Icelandic Center for Language Technology, and the latest release holds about 2,233 hours of recordings.

It also released the Althingi parliamentary corpus of about 542 hours covering 2005 to 2016, the first public Icelandic corpus of children's voices, and synthetic data generated with its TTS systems. The datasets and models are licensed openly on Hugging Face, OpenSLR and LDC.
mission: To make Icelandic speech technology openly available, with large corpora and models for recognition and synthesis.

It runs the National Language Technologies Portal and maintains Welsh speech recognition, text-to-speech, translation and terminology tools. Its public repositories date back to 2014, and it has worked with Welsh Common Voice, the Welsh government and S4C.

tagline: Lightly is a Zurich company, born from ETH research, that open-sources self-supervised learning and vision training libraries.
about: Lightly was founded by Matthias Heller and Igor Susmelj as a data-centric AI company based on ETH Zurich research. It raised a 3 million dollar seed round in May 2022 and reports 10 million dollars raised in total.

Its open-source lightly library for self-supervised learning dates from October 2020. It later added the labelformat converter, LightlyTrain for vision model pretraining and distillation, and LightlyStudio, alongside a commercial platform.
mission: To help teams build better vision models by improving the data that models are trained on.

tagline: LINAGORA is a French open-source software company behind the LinTO voice assistant and the Lucie French open LLM.
about: LINAGORA was founded in 2000 by Alexandre Zapolsky and Michel-Marie Maudet, and its headquarters moved to Issy-les-Moulineaux in 2024. Its products include Twake Workplace, OpenPaaS and the LinTO voice assistant, and its GitHub organization holds more than 500 repositories.

In 2023 it created the OpenLLM France community, and in January 2025 it released Lucie, an open-source sovereign large language model. The release drew criticism after tests of an unfinished version and was temporarily suspended.
mission: To invent and develop ethical, open-source technology and to support open sovereign AI in France.

about: MaiNLP is a research lab at the Center for Information and Language Processing at LMU Munich. It is led by Barbara Plank, who holds the Chair for AI and Computational Linguistics and co-directs the center.

Its research addresses robustness to language variation, fairness and human label variation, and it runs the ERC project DIALECT. The lab belongs to the ELLIS Europe NLP Program and ELLIS Unit Munich, and publishes datasets such as CrossRE and a survey of Germanic low-resource corpora on GitHub.

Models trained on Europeana newspapers cover German, French and historic multilingual text, with German BERT released in February 2020. All models are MIT-licensed on Hugging Face under the dbmdz organization.
